item.title: U.S. Loses Its Measles Elimination Status, a Historic Setback for American Health
item.description: The nation was once regarded as a global leader for reining in the highly contagious virus. Now, large outbreaks that sicken thousands could become routine.
item.dc:creator: Teddy Rosenbluth
item.media:credit: Rachel Wisniewski for The New York Times

item.title: Measles Is Officially Back in the United States. What Now?
item.description: It will take years for the country to regain elimination status. In the meantime, communities will need to adopt numerous strategies to protect people.
item.dc:creator: Apoorva Mandavilli and Dani Blum
item.media:credit: Desiree Rios for The New York Times
item.media:description: A patient with a measles rash in Texas last year. The number of cases in the United States this year has topped 5,400, more than double last year’s tally and the highest since 1991, nearly a decade before the country attained elimination status.

item.title: Do You Need a Measles Booster?
item.description: As cases spread across North America, now is a good time to check your vaccination status.
item.dc:creator: Dani Blum

item.title: Ukraine Attacks Kerch Bridge Linking Russia to Occupied Crimea
item.description: Destroying the structure, the only one connecting Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, has long been a top objective for Kyiv.
item.dc:creator: Marc Santora and James McManagan
item.media:description: Workers cutting electrical wires on the Southern Bridge in Kyiv, which was damaged in an overnight strike.

item.title: Leaked Records Show Deutsche Bank Courting Russian Oligarchs

item.title: As Trump and Xi Mingle, Their Governments Are Arming Up

item.title: President Trump Starts Asia Trip With Quick Manila Stopover
item.description: Even for a president who prizes photo opportunities, Mr. Trump’s appearance in Manila suggested a lack of interest in diplomatic wins or issues at home. ‘It’s life,’ he said.
item.dc:creator: Katie Rogers and David E. Sanger
item.media:description: President Trump arriving in Manila on Tuesday. He was quickly taken to his hotel, where several world leaders had gathered to bring the diplomatic summit to his doorstep.

item.title: Trump Administration Divide on China Policy Breaks Into Public View
item.description: The airing of a fight over advanced A.I. chips shows how much the Nvidia scandal has deepened fissures inside the government, just as President Trump heads to a critical meeting with his Chinese counterpart.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Swan, Maggie Haberman, Ana Swanson and Shawn McCreesh
item.category: Ministry of State Security of the People's Republic of China
Far East, South and Southeast Asia and Pacific Areas
item.media:description: President Trump acknowledged on Monday that the Treasury and commerce secretaries had been at odds over how hard to crack down on a loophole that has allowed China to access advanced A.I. chips through data centers in other countries.

item.title: Tracking China’s War of Words Against Japan
item.description: Beijing is running a concerted campaign to paint Japan as an aggressor and resurgent military threat, according to a Times analysis.
item.dc:creator: Javier C. Hernández and Gal Koplewitz
item.media:description: A headline in the Global Times, a newspaper controlled by China’s ruling Communist Party, about Japan’s “remilitarization” after China restricted exports to Japanese entities.

item.title: School Phone Bans Are Gradually Improving Test Scores, New Evidence Shows
item.description: Previous results were mixed, but the first national study to track individual students’ growth shows bans may help reverse declines.
item.dc:creator: Claire Cain Miller
item.media:credit: Photo Illustration by Tonje Thilesen for The New York Times
item.media:description: The study showed gains in both math and reading, for students at all levels of achievement.

item.title: As Trump Goes to China, A.I. Tensions Surge Amid Spying and Safety Fears

item.title: Debt Problems of the Richest Countries Are Trickling Down to the Poorest

item.media:description: A market in Daloa, western Ivory Coast. Ivory Coast, Kenya and Nigeria have pledged annual interest rates of 7.5 to more than 10 percent to lenders.

item.title: Shoe Prices Hit a Record High Amid Inflation and Increased Tariffs
item.description: Shoe prices have been rising faster than overall prices in recent months, and there’s little sign those increases will reverse soon.
item.dc:creator: Kim Bhasin
item.media:description: The jump in the price of shoes reached a record high this year as footwear companies pushed elevated costs on to American consumers.
